:::note[About this page]
This page is generated from the `tools/list` response of [s1000d-verify-mcp](/s1000d-stack/mcp/verify-mcp/) 0.10.0. The s1000d-verify-mcp page explains the configuration and how to read the responses.

## Summary

Runs the same verification as `verify_data_module` and returns candidate corrections for each finding. The server decides the candidates and adds where they come from and how certain they are (`exact` / `several` / `none`). If `product` is given, applicability that cannot be decided because the product lacks a value also gets candidate values. It does not apply any correction to the document

## Description returned by `tools/list`

This is the text an LLM receives.

> Verify one data module (same steps as verify_data_module) and return fix candidates for each finding: XSD errors (values and elements from the libxml2 message or from the XSD definitions), BREX violations (the rule's allowed values with their descriptions; remove / add for forbidden / missing; allowed notations), unresolved references (similar DMCs in the CSDB, the issue present in the CSDB, ICN files that differ only in the extension, similar ids) and, when "product" is given, applicability that cannot be decided because the product lacks a value (values from the ACT, CCT and PCT). Every candidate is decided by the server; each fix has a confidence (exact / several / none) and the source of its candidates. Does NOT apply any fix.

## Arguments

The content of `inputSchema`. A nested argument is written as `parent.child`, and an item of an array as `parent[].child`.

| Name | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` |  |  | File path of the data module (or PM) to check. |
| `xml` | `string` |  |  | The document as an XML string (alternative to path; max 5 MB). |
| `csdbDirs` | `array<string>` |  |  | CSDB folders to search for referenced data modules, publication modules, ICN files and BREX (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file; BREX is also searched under S1000D_SPEC_DIR). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes. |
| `skip` | `array<string>` |  |  | Steps to skip. Skipped steps are reported with state "not-run". |
| `product` | `object` |  |  | The product to evaluate applicability against. If given, applicability that is undetermined because the product lacks a value is reported with candidate values. Omit it to skip applicability. |
| `product.attributes` | `object` |  |  | ACT productAttribute id → value. |
| `product.conditions` | `object` |  |  | CCT cond id → value. |
| `includeSpecificationReferences` | `boolean` |  | default `false` | Also list fixes for dmRef to the S1000D specification itself (modelIdentCode "S1000D"). They are never in a CSDB, are not errors and carry no candidate (default false; the count is always returned). |
| `maxFixes` | `number` |  | default `200` | Cap on fixes returned (default 200). The total count is always reported. |
| `maxCandidates` | `number` |  | default `20` | Cap on candidates per fix (default 20). A fix that was cut carries candidateCount. |
